figures.caption:
\label{fig:summary}
Summary of the main results and related results from the literature. $G$ is a signed digraph on $[n]$, and $f$ is a BN on $G$. $\fp(f)$ is the number of fixed points of $f$. $\att(f)$ is the number of asynchronous attractors of $f$, that is, the number of inclusion-minimal set $A\subseteq\B^n$ such that $f^i(A)\subseteq A$ for every $i\in [n]$. We have $\att(f)\geq 1$ and $\att(f)\geq \fp(f)$ since $x$ is a fixed point of $f$ if and only if $\{x\}$ is an asynchronous attractor of $f$. $f$ is unstable if, for all $i\in [n]$ and $x\in\B^n$, we have $f^w(x)_i\neq x_i$ for some word~$w$ (conclusion of Lemma~\ref{lem:flipping_lemma}). $\fix(f)$ is the minimum length of a word $w$ over $[n]$ such that $f^w(x)$ is a fixed point of $f$ for any $x\in\B^n$; if no such word exists then $\fix(f)=\infty$. $\synch(f)$ is the minimum length of a synchronizing word for $f$; if no such word exists then $\synch(f)=\infty$.
